narrative.overview: Redline is a proofreader's red pen taken to the contract a client just handed you. The page is not a product tour or a dashboard; it is a sheet of manila proofing paper with a ruled margin, typewriter ink, and correction marks made by hand in the margin. The manila field (#e7e0d0) owns every surface — it is the page, not a background behind cards. Depth comes from lifting a sheet slightly brighter than the one beneath it, never from a slab of color dropped onto white. The system refuses two defaults it was built against: the legaltech-SaaS look (navy gradient, floating app screenshot, "AI-powered" badge) and the cream-serif law-firm look. Everything here reads as a physical artifact being corrected. Color is load-bearing, not decorative: a red mark on this page always means a clause that can hurt you; it is never used to brighten a button or draw an idle eye. That restraint is the product's credibility expressed as a palette rule.
keyCharacteristics: Manila proofing paper is the field; sheets lift by tone, never by shadow-on-white.
Hard corners everywhere (0 radius); the artifact is cut and stamped, not rounded.
Typewriter mono display headlines; serif body; letterpress small-caps labels; a red pen hand for margin marks.
One authored motion moment: the red pen circling and striking the dangerous line.
Semantic color is an invariant: red = danger, blue = a missing protection, amber = bounded caution.

rules.name: The Red-Means-Danger Rule
rules.body: Red (#c01f1f / #8a1616) is reserved for danger only — Critical findings, the Walk-away verdict, and proof marks. It never decorates a surface, a hover, or a non-danger CTA's background for decoration's sake. If a red element does not mean "this can hurt you," it is wrong. Audit test: every red pixel on a screen must trace to a Critical/Walk-away finding or a proof mark.

rules.name: The Three-Signal Rule
rules.body: The three correction colors are a fixed semantic triad: red = danger, blue = a missing protection (Gap), amber = bounded caution. A finding's color is decided by its meaning, never by visual balance. Never recolor a tier to even out a layout.

rules.name: The Warm-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is warm ink (#574f3d), never a cool gray. The page is aged paper; a gray would read as screen chrome and break the artifact.

rules.name: The Document-Voice Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime is reserved for two jobs: typewriter display headlines, and anything that is literally the document's own words (the galley text, the cited sentence, the counter-offer). Never set running prose in mono — that is Spectral's job.

rules.name: The Pen-Hand Rule
rules.body: Caveat (the red pen hand) appears only as a margin correction mark. It is never used for a heading, a label, or body copy; it is the human hand writing in the margin, and overusing it dissolves that meaning.

rules.name: The Tonal-Lift Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by paper tone first; shadow is only for the two hero objects (the galley and the specimen). Do not reach for a shadow where a brighter sheet tone will read the layer.

rules.name: The Soft-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft, warm, and far-cast (large blur, negative spread). No hard zero-blur offset shadows — the hard edges live in the corners and borders, not the shadows.

dos: Do keep red (#c01f1f) for danger only — Critical findings, the Walk-away verdict, and proof marks. The primary CTA is the sole red-filled surface, and only because it is itself a danger stamp.
Do separate layers by paper tone first (#e7e0d0 → #efe9da → #f4efe2), reaching for a soft warm shadow only on the galley and specimen hero objects.
Do set the document's own words — galley text, cited sentences, counter-offers — in Courier Prime, and running prose in Spectral.
Do draw proof marks as authored SVG sharing one pen weight (stroke-width 2.4, round caps/joins), so every red mark looks made by one pen.
Do cut corners square (0 radius) and define containers with hairline or dashed rules.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: the circle and strike settle to their finished state with no animation.
donts: Don't use red to brighten a button background, a hover, a divider, or any element that does not mean "this can hurt you."
Don't recolor a finding's tier (red/amber/blue) to balance a layout — the color is fixed by meaning.
Don't use a cool gray for secondary text or borders; the neutrals are warm paper tones (warm secondary ink #574f3d).
Don't add hard zero-blur offset shadows; shadows stay soft and far-cast even though corners are hard. This is not a neobrutalist world.
Don't set running prose in Courier Prime, or use the Caveat pen hand for anything but a margin correction mark.
Don't round corners or drop a colored card onto a white field — the manila paper is the page.
